turns.query: Form 13F filings carry a cover page whose value total is stated separately from the individual holding rows. Work with holdings reports only, excluding notice filings and every amendment, and keep filings that report both a positive cover-page value total and a positive holding-row count. For the quarters ending 2022-09-30 and 2022-12-31 report the number of qualifying filings in each. For each quarter compute every filing's cover-page value total divided by its holding-row count and report the median of that quantity, then report the later quarter's median divided by the earlier one and, separately, the later quarter's summed cover-page totals divided by the earlier quarter's. Explain what the size of these two ratios says about whether the change between the quarters is an economic one.

Stay with the qualifying filings for the quarter ending 2022-12-31. The governed table records, for each filing, the reporting unit inferred from its holding rows. For this exercise, classify the cover-page field separately as thousands scale when its reported value total divided by its holding-row count is below 100,000 reported units, and as dollar scale otherwise. Report how many filings the holding-row classification marks as dollars and how many as thousands, how many the cover-page heuristic marks as each, how many filings the two classifications disagree on, and how many of those report holding rows in dollars while the cover-page heuristic reads as thousands scale. Explain what the disagreement count means for using one inferred classification to rescale the other field, and identify the 100,000 cut as an analytic heuristic rather than source metadata or a consequence of the Form 13F filing threshold.

Turn to the issuer-level aggregation, in which holdings are already restated into dollars from each filing's own holding-row unit. For the quarter ending 2022-12-31 report the number of issuer rows and their total reported value in USD trillions. Identify the issuer with the largest reported value, breaking a tie by CUSIP ascending, and report its CUSIP, its issuer name as the aggregation records it, its reported value in USD trillions and how many filers report it. Then report the numerical quotient of that USD aggregation total divided by the summed raw cover-page values you computed for the same quarter in turn 1. Explain why the quotient is not a unit-consistent ratio and which aggregation can support a dollar statement.

Bridge the leading issuer from turn 3 to the registrant universe. Match it to the registrant whose name equals the issuer name once both are compared in lower case with characters other than letters, digits and spaces removed, and report that registrant's ticker. Take the registrant's cover-page count of common shares outstanding, using the latest such count filed on or before 2023-02-15, and report the share count together with its as-of date. Report the shares the issuer aggregation records for the quarter, and those shares as a percent of shares outstanding. Then report how many of the quarter's qualifying filings include other managers' holdings and the largest number of other managers included on any one of them. Explain what the percent does and does not establish about institutional ownership of this issuer.
